claims.asserted_formula: [D] != 0 iff p^(-e) adj(A) C is not integral; Inn is a proper submodule of Der
claims.replacement: For n=p^k, k>=2 and e=v_p(|v-u|), [D] != 0 iff adj(A)C/p^(p^e) is not integral. Nonzero outer classes exist for every distinct twist pair. The printed vector is integral for every derivation.
claims.proof: Proposition 1, Theorem 2 and Corollary 3 in note.tex

claims.asserted_formula: D is inner iff p^(-e) adj(A)C is integral; p^e dividing all coordinates suffices; p dividing all coordinates suffices
claims.replacement: D is inner iff adj(A)C/p^(p^e) is integral. Divisibility by p always suffices; divisibility by p^e suffices for e>=1 but not for e=0.
claims.boundary_example: n=9, u=1, v=2, D(zeta)=1; e=0 and the multiplier vector has denominator three.

claims.replacement: In the fixed same-domain/codomain power basis, det(A)=p^(p^e)>0.
claims.proof: Corollary 3; the arithmetic Smith form specializes Noferini–Williams 2024, Theorem 3.11.

claims.asserted_formula: Three determinant cases for n=2^r*q; corresponding adjugate innerness tests and coordinate divisibility conditions
claims.replacement: For |v-u|=2^a*q^b*m, gcd(m,2q)=1, determinants are 2^(2^a*(q-1)) if 1<=a<r and b>=1, q^(2^(r-1)) if a>=r and b=0, and 1 otherwise. Coordinate rank is N=2^(r-1)*(q-1). The prime 2 or q suffices for coordinate divisibility in the first or second case.
claims.proof: Corollary 6; arithmetic is a specialization of Noferini–Williams 2026, Theorems 2.2 and 2.4.

claims.asserted_formula: Outer classes are detected by the corresponding nonintegral adjugate vector, with nonzero outer classes in the two nonunit determinant cases and none otherwise
claims.replacement: Use rank N=2^(r-1)*(q-1), and replace the unbound i in part (i) by a=e_1. The determinant denominators and all existence/nonexistence clauses then follow from the quotient theorem.
claims.proof: Corollary 6; the undefined printed index is not assigned a numerical truth value.

claims.locator: Section 3.2, Conjectures 3.12–3.13, p. 18; also v1, pp. 15–16
claims.asserted_formula: For odd prime conductor, det(A)=p; D is inner iff adj(A)C/p is integral; p dividing all coordinates suffices; nonzero outer classes exist
claims.replacement: All assertions hold, and Out is additively Z/pZ.
claims.proof: Corollary 4; the determinant and Smith form specialize Noferini–Williams 2024, Theorem 3.11.

claims.locator: Theorem 4.2(ii), pp. 7–9; already present in v1, pp. 6–8
claims.asserted_formula: For squarefree s=1 mod 4 and D(theta)=alpha+beta*theta, beta even implies innerness
claims.replacement: For s!=1, theta=(1+sqrt(s))/2, innerness is equivalent to s dividing 2*alpha+beta. The criterion is equivalent to Manju–Sharma's Theorem 3.5, present in December 2024.
claims.counterexample: s=-3, theta=zeta_6, D(theta)=1: beta=0 is even but the multiplier coordinates are (-1/3,2/3).
claims.proof: Corollary 5; exact prior replacement in https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.03500v1, Theorem 3.5, p. 11, and v3, p. 13.

claims.statement: For arbitrary n>=3, Out=O/(zeta^v-zeta^u)O; it is additively (Z/ell Z)^(phi(n)/phi(h)) for h=n/gcd(n,|v-u|) a power of ell, and zero otherwise.
claims.proof: Theorem 2 supplies an elementary alternative norm proof of the arithmetic specialization and identifies the derivation quotient.

claims.statement: Every distinct twist pair has nonzero outer classes iff n is a prime power or twice an odd prime power.
claims.proof: Corollary 7; the converse uses u=1, v=n-1, with h=n/gcd(n,2).

written_scope: The arbitrary-conductor quotient, cyclotomic Smith form, corrected criteria, quadratic criterion and all-pairs conductor classification have complete written proofs in the note.
finite_scope: Exact checks cover the two quadratic laws, Gaussian vectors, the conductor-nine example, and all 1338 unordered distinct unit pairs at the stated 24 conductors, with maximum degree 24.
